questions.q: Which iconic building at De La Salle University in Manila is considered one of Tomas Mapua's greatest neoclassical masterpieces?
questions.n: Constructed in the 1920s, this H-shaped neoclassical building is Mapua's most famous institutional work.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua designed the Nurse's Home for which major medical institution in Manila?
questions.n: Mapua designed the Nurse's Home at PGH, contributing to the complex's overall campus plan.

questions.q: In the Tondo district of Manila, Mapua is credited with the design of which historic community hospital?
questions.n: Mapua designed the architectural structure for this hospital, which has served the Tondo community since the early 1900s.

questions.q: Which of these features is a hallmark of Mapua's design for the St. La Salle Hall?
o: Exposed steel beams and industrial finish
questions.n: The use of classical orders like Corinthian columns is central to the neoclassical style Mapua employed for institutional buildings.

questions.q: Mapua served as a supervising architect for which government body, overseeing the design of numerous school buildings (Gabaldon types)?
questions.n: Mapua worked here as a supervising architect, where he influenced the design of public infrastructure across the islands.

questions.q: The Mapua Institute of Technology (now Mapua University) moved to its iconic campus in Intramuros later, but which style did Mapua generally champion for his educational institutions?
questions.n: Mapua utilized neoclassical principles to give educational buildings a sense of dignity, order, and permanence.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Mapua was involved in the design of the Philippine Normal University (PNU) campus.
questions.n: As a supervising architect in the Bureau of Public Works, Mapua had oversight and design input on various normal schools and government hubs.

questions.q: Which of Mapua's projects is distinguished by its 'H-shape' plan to allow for maximum natural ventilation and light?
questions.n: The H-shaped layout was a deliberate choice by Mapua to ensure airflow and lighting for the classrooms and offices.

questions.q: Before establishing his own practice and school, Mapua worked on the design of several 'Gabaldon' schools. What is a 'Gabaldon' school?
questions.n: These were standard designs for public schools across the Philippines, often incorporating bahay kubo and bahay na bato elements for ventilation.

questions.q: Mapua's legacy in construction materials is often linked to his family's business. What did the Mapua family's company produce?
questions.n: The Mapua family owned a famous factory (Mapua Tiles) that produced high-quality encaustic cement tiles.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua is famously known for holding which professional license number in the Philippines?
questions.n: As the first registered architect under Act No. 2985, he was issued the very first license in the country.

questions.q: Which city in the United States did Tomas Mapua travel to for his high school education before entering Cornell University?
questions.n: Mapua attended Boone’s Preparatory School in Wilmington, Delaware, to prepare for his university studies.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Mapua was the only Filipino architect to be sent to the United States under the Pensionado program.
questions.n: Mapua was part of a larger cohort of talented Filipinos sent to master various professional disciplines in America.

questions.q: In what year did Tomas Mapua return to the Philippines after completing his architectural studies at Cornell?
questions.n: Mapua returned in 1911 and immediately began working for the Bureau of Public Works.

questions.q: What was the primary reason Tomas Mapua founded the Mapua Institute of Technology?
o: To provide technical education to Filipinos
To create a school specifically for the arts
questions.n: He wanted to ensure that Filipinos had access to high-quality training in architecture and engineering to build the nation.

questions.q: Which specific architectural order is prominently featured on the facade of St. La Salle Hall at De La Salle University?
questions.n: The building's neoclassical grandeur is emphasized by the use of Corinthian columns, recognized by their acanthus leaf capitals.

questions.q: While working at the Bureau of Public Works, Tomas Mapua was often tasked with supervising the design of schools. What was the primary climate-responsive feature of these 'Gabaldon' designs?
o: Thick stone walls for thermal mass
Small openings to keep out the sun
questions.n: These features were integrated to promote natural cross-ventilation and protect the structure from seasonal flooding.

questions.q: What is the primary material used for the exterior finish of many of Mapua's neoclassical government buildings?
questions.n: Mapua utilized modern reinforced concrete, often finished with plaster to mimic the appearance of traditional stone masonry.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua's design for the Mary Johnston Hospital in Tondo is significant because it represents:
o: The first high-rise hospital in Asia
A project entirely funded by his family company
The introduction of the Brutalist style
An early example of institutional architecture for social welfare
questions.n: This project highlighted his involvement in designing spaces dedicated to public health and charitable service.

questions.q: Before his formal registration in 1921, in which government office did Mapua gain the most experience in public infrastructure?
o: The City Planning Office of Manila
questions.n: He served as a supervising architect here for several years, which established his reputation before he went into private practice.

questions.q: Act No. 2985, passed in 1921, was the legislation that allowed Mapua to become the first registered architect. What was the primary purpose of this act?
o: To mandate the use of concrete in all public buildings
To regulate the practice of architecture and engineering in the Philippines
To establish the University of the Philippines College of Architecture
To fund the construction of the Manila Central Post Office
questions.n: It established the board of examiners and required formal registration for those practicing these technical professions.

questions.q: The 'Mapua Tiles' produced by his family's factory are a type of which architectural finish?
questions.n: These are hand-made, patterned cement tiles where the color is part of the material layer, not just a surface paint.

questions.q: In the H-shaped layout of St. La Salle Hall, what was the primary functional advantage for the students and faculty?
o: To minimize the use of construction materials
Enhanced cross-ventilation and natural lighting for every room
Maximum security through limited entry points
A layout designed specifically for secret passageways
questions.n: The thin wings of the 'H' ensure that every classroom has windows on at least two sides, crucial for tropical comfort.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua was a co-founder of the first professional organization for architects in the country. What was this organization?
questions.n: Mapua was a founding member of the PIA (originally the Philippine Architects’ Society), established in 1933.

questions.q: Which of these neoclassical elements is NOT a primary feature of Mapua's institutional works?
questions.n: Asymmetry and large cantilevers are hallmarks of Modernism and Brutalism, which came after Mapua's prime.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua's alma mater, Cornell University, is located in which city and state?
questions.n: Mapua graduated from this Ivy League institution in 1911, which was a significant center for architectural education at the time.

questions.q: Which fellow Pensionado and architect was a contemporary of Mapua at the Bureau of Public Works and is known for the Legislative Building?
questions.n: Toledo was a key contemporary who, along with Juan Arellano, worked alongside Mapua during the American colonial period.

questions.q: The St. La Salle Hall uses which specific architectural style that was the hallmark of American colonial 'City Beautiful' planning?
questions.n: This style combined classical Greek and Roman forms with modern materials like reinforced concrete, a hallmark of Mapua's major works.

questions.q: In the production of Mapua Encaustic Tiles, how is the colorful pattern achieved?
o: Digital printing on a ceramic base
Inlaying different colors of liquid clay or cement into a mold
questions.n: The pattern is created by pouring colored cement mixtures into brass dividers within a mold, ensuring the design lasts as the tile wears.

questions.q: What was Mapua's official title when he served the government in the Bureau of Public Works?
questions.n: He held this high-ranking position, allowing him to oversee the design and construction of various public projects across the country.

questions.q: The Philippine Architects’ Society, which Mapua co-founded, was the precursor to which modern-day organization?
o: Department of Public Works and Highways
questions.n: Founded in 1933 with Mapua as a key figure, the PAS was renamed the PIA in 1945.

questions.q: Which of Mapua's works served as the first headquarters for the Mapua Institute of Technology in 1925?
o: The Bureau of Public Works Building
A rented wing in the St. La Salle Hall
questions.n: The school was established as a formal educational institution in a commercial/residential building in Quiapo.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua's design philosophy for schools emphasized the 'Gabaldon' type. What was a key structural material used in the roofs of these schools?
questions.n: These became the standard for Gabaldon schools because they were durable, fire-resistant, and easier to install in large quantities.

questions.q: Before Act No. 2985 was passed in 1921, how were architects in the Philippines generally recognized?
o: There were no architects in the country
They were licensed by the Spanish Crown
They were only recognized if they studied in Europe
They were all considered Civil Engineers
questions.n: Prior to the specific architecture act, many practiced under a general 'Master of Works' or engineering designation.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua passed away in 1965. In his later years, he saw his school become a leader in which fields?
questions.n: Mapua Institute of Technology solidified its reputation as a premier institution for these two specific technical disciplines.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua was born in which historic district of Manila, known for its rich trade history?
questions.n: Born in 1888, Mapua grew up in this district, which was the heart of the Chinese-Filipino community and commerce.

questions.q: What was the name of the preparatory school in Wilmington, Delaware, that Mapua attended to prepare for university?
questions.n: He attended this school to bridge his Filipino education with the requirements of an American Ivy League university.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Mapua was the very first Filipino to graduate from an American school with a degree in Architecture.
questions.n: Upon graduating from Cornell in 1911, he became the first Filipino to earn a formal US architectural degree.

questions.q: In neoclassical architecture, what do you call the triangular gable found above the entablature of a building like St. La Salle Hall?
questions.n: The pediment is the characteristic triangular shape that often contains sculptures or reliefs in classical designs.

questions.q: Mapua’s family business, which produced encaustic tiles, was named what?
questions.n: This is a common naming convention, but his tile business was specifically known as the 'Mapua Concrete Tile Factory'.

questions.q: What was the main purpose of the H-shaped floor plan in early 20th-century schools like those designed by Mapua?
o: To separate the male and female students
To allow for better air circulation and light
questions.n: The thin 'wings' of the H ensured that classrooms had windows on both sides, allowing for passive cooling.

questions.q: In what decade did Tomas Mapua establish the Mapua Institute of Technology?
questions.n: The school was founded in 1925, shortly after the passage of the professional registration act.

questions.q: Which material is 'Encaustic' tile specifically made of, distinguishing it from ceramic?
questions.n: These tiles are made of hydraulic cement and colorful minerals, pressed into a mold without firing.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua’s style is often called 'Beaux-Arts'. Where did this term originate?
questions.n: It refers to the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris, which taught a grand, ornamental, and classical style of design.

questions.q: Before he was an architect, Tomas Mapua was briefly interested in which other creative field?
questions.n: He was an excellent painter and illustrator, skills that eventually led him to the drafting tables of architecture.
